support.title: Support the Project
support.intro: Project NOMAD is 100% free and open source — no subscriptions, no paywalls, no catch. If you'd like to help keep the project going, here are a few ways to show your support.

coffee.title: Buy Us a Coffee
coffee.description: Every contribution helps fund development, server costs, and new content packs for NOMAD. Even a small donation goes a long way.

network.title: Need Help With Your Home Network?
network.alt: Rogue Support — Conquer Your Home Network
network.description: Rogue Support is a networking consultation service for home users. Think of it as Uber for computer networking — expert help when you need it.

other.title: Other Ways to Help
other.starSuffix: it helps more people discover NOMAD
other.share: Share NOMAD with someone who'd use it — word of mouth is the best marketing
other.discordSuffix: hang out, share your build, help other users

creatorPacks.intro: Install branded video collections from creators. Packs download in the background and play offline through Kiwix.

connectionLost.message: You may see error notifications while the backend restarts during the update. This is completely normal and expected. Connection should be restored momentarily.

models.flashDesc: Enables OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 for improved memory efficiency. Disable if you experience instability. Takes effect after reinstalling the {{name}}.
models.thinking: Use thinking automatically when a model supports it
models.thinkingDesc: Sets the default for models that can think. You can still turn thinking on or off for an individual model in the chat window.
models.ragDesc: Search your knowledge base for relevant documents before answering. Turn this off to save memory and speed up replies when your knowledge base is small or empty. This is the same switch as the one in the chat window.
models.name: Assistant Name
models.nameHelp: Give your AI assistant a custom name that will be used in the chat interface and other areas of the application.
models.tasksModelHelp: Small, fast model used for background work like chat titles and suggestions. Leave this set to the chat model to use whichever model the chat is using. Avoid reasoning models here — they are slow at short, aesthetic tasks.
models.relevanceHelp: How closely a knowledge-base passage has to match your question before it is used in an answer. Stricter settings keep unrelated passages out; too strict and genuinely useful ones get dropped too. When nothing clears the bar, the assistant answers from its own knowledge instead.
models.relCheckDesc: Before answering, ask the Tasks Model whether the passages found are actually about your question, and leave them out (and uncited) when they are not. Helps most with large libraries like Wikipedia or Project Gutenberg, where something always looks similar. Needs a capable Tasks Model (about 8B parameters or larger); smaller models reject too many good matches. Adds a short delay to every reply.
models.styleHelp: How adventurous the assistant is when picking its next word. Auto follows whatever the model's author recommended and fills in the rest, and suits most people. Focused gives shorter, steadier, more repeatable answers and is the better choice for looking things up. Creative varies its wording more, at some cost to accuracy.
models.contextHelp: How much conversation and knowledge-base context each reply can consider. Auto sizes this per model from its trained limit and your available memory. Choosing a value sets an upper limit — it can lower the window to save memory, but never raises it beyond what a model supports.
models.inEffectNote: Changes take effect for new conversations.
models.noneInstalled: No models installed. Browse the model catalog below to get started.
models.remoteHelp: Connect to any OpenAI-compatible API server — Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and others are all supported. For remote Ollama instances, the host must be started with <c>OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0</c>.
models.remoteUrlPh: http://192.168.1.100:11434  (or :1234 for OpenAI API Compatible Apps)

autoUpd.appDesc: Automatically install minor and patch updates for apps you've opted in (toggle each app in Supply Depot). Major versions always require a manual update. Uses the same update window and cool-off period as the core schedule above.

autoUpd.capInvalid: Data cap must be 0 or a positive number of GB.
autoUpd.contentSaveFail: Failed to save content update schedule.
autoUpd.contentDisabledMsg: Automatic content updates were disabled after repeated failures.
autoUpd.contentDesc: Automatically download newer versions of your installed Information Library content (ZIM files) and maps during your chosen window. Content downloads can be very large, so set a per-window data cap to limit how much is pulled at once. We recommend allowing at least 0.5 GB per update window to ensure most updates can be pulled in a timely manner, but you can set a lower cap if you have very limited bandwidth and don't mind some updates being skipped (they will still appear in the UI and can be updated manually). If an update repeatedly fails to download within the window, it will be automatically disabled and require manual intervention to re-enable.

autoUpd.allUpToDate: All installed content is up to date. New versions will appear here when detected.
autoUpd.skippedCap: Skipped — exceeds data cap, update manually

autoUpd.allUpMsg: All your installed content is running the latest available version.
autoUpd.coreDisabledMsg: Automatic core updates were disabled after repeated failures.
autoUpd.coreDesc: Automatically install minor and patch updates during your chosen window. Major versions always require a manual update due to their potentially breaking nature.
autoUpd.coreDelay: Delay after a release is published
autoUpd.noEligible: No eligible update — system is current or the latest release is a major version / still in cool-off.
